items.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: We worked with Bob Stewart in that big orchestra in Switzerland. Bob Stewart the tuba player.

ctx.x: I’m so glad you said that because I had a professor recently ask my opinion, why was it, especially in the forties and fifties, so many of these well known jazz musicians are connected with the drug scene? And I didn’t really have an answer for him. I mean you can say well they work in bars and nightclubs. But there’s got to be something more than that.

First of all it started with the whole racial thing. Billie Holiday had to go through the kitchen in the hotel because she was black, and so on and so on. So that started it. Second, if you aren’t strong, and you become well known, and you are king on stage, and then you have to go home and pay your phone bill, you have to do the daily grind, and if you aren’t strong personally you will go on drugs. We worked with Bob Stewart in that big orchestra in Switzerland. Bob Stewart the tuba player.
